speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: asked the Minister for Trade and Industry (a) what are the reasons for providing Marina Bay Sands and Resorts World Sentosa with the option to increase their Approved Gaming Area by 2,000 square meters and 500 square meters respectively; (b) whether a study has been carried out to examine whether an increase in gaming area would cause a rise in problem gambling; and (c) what further measures will be put in place to help ensure that problem gambling will be deterred.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
text: asked the Minister for Trade and Industry (a) how much land has been allocated for the proposed expansion of MBS and RWS; (b) how much will MBS and RWS be paying for the land; and (c) how much additional land cost will each have to pay for the expansion of the gaming areas of the casinos.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: The business model of an Integrated Resort (IR) combines a controlled proportion of gaming activities with a wide range of high-quality non-gaming amenities, such as theatres, theme parks, museums, hotels, Meetings, Incentives, Conferences and Exhibitions (MICE) facilities, restaurants and retail shops.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Gaming activities are an important source of revenue for the operators, contributing more than two-thirds of their total revenue.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: The gaming revenue makes it commercially viable for them to offer the non-gaming facilities, as one integrated package.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: The two IRs have not decided to activate their additional gaming options.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: The IRs have also stated that the additional gaming provisions will be targeted at higher tier, non-mass market players, who are mostly tourists.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Based on the Gambling Participation Survey conducted by the National Council on Problem Gambling (NCPG), the probable problem and pathological gambling rate of Singapore residents has decreased from 2.6% in 2011 to 0.9% in 2017.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: This includes all forms of gambling, such as casino, horse racing and online gambling.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: The Government takes a serious view on tackling problem gambling and will continue to work closely with our community partners to help affected individuals and families.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: We had discussed with them before making the announcement.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: The Government will also be strengthening our social safeguards.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: The investments will also create up to 5,000 new jobs directly and increase business opportunities for Singapore companies.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: When there are substantial investments that can benefit our economy and our workers, the Government is open to directly allocate land to these investors.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: This is a long-standing policy that has been extended to both local and foreign companies across different industries.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: The IRs will pay fair market value for their land, as determined by the Chief Valuer in accordance with market conditions and established valuation principles.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Resorts World Sentosa has set aside a budget of $1 billion to intensify the use of existing land and purchase around one hectare of new land.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: If the IRs choose to activate their options for additional gaming area, they will have to pay additional costs for these areas.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: The amount payable will be determined by the Chief Valuer based on prevailing market conditions when the option is exercised.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: As the Minister for Finance had explained at Budget 2018 and Budget 2019, Singapore's healthcare spending will rise with an ageing population and advances in medical treatment, drugs and technologies.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: We need to be well-prepared for this, by building additional healthcare capacity and ensuring that we have sufficient financial resources to fund the higher healthcare spending in a sustainable manner.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: This will require a structural increase in our operating revenue.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Our revenue base is diverse and resilient, including taxes on personal and corporate income, consumption and property.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: The tax revenue from the two IRs is one of the many sources of overall tax revenue.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: The diverse sources of revenue are supported by a diversified economy.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: As we continue to grow Singapore's economy, we will adopt a multi-pronged strategy, with many different sectors and trading partners.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: So, am I correct to say that if the gaming area is not expanded, then the world-class attractions would be projected to be loss-making?

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: The IR business model, as I explained in my answer, means it is an integrated package.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: You need the gaming activities to come together with the non-gaming activities so that it is commercially viable for the operators.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Currently, more than two-thirds of their total revenue come from gaming.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: So, for the new facilities, the theme parks, the 15,000-seater arena, these are expensive facilities which, without the gaming provisions, the additional gaming provisions as options for the operators, they may not find it commercially viable to make these additional investments to create these additional jobs.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: This was actually explained by the Chief Executive Officer of MBS and I quote him, he said, "The casino revenue generation is very important because it pays for things that sometimes lose money, sometimes have a very low return, or that are just very expensive."

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Just to clarify with the Senior Minister of State, Mr Speaker.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: On the second part of my question, prior to the approvals, were any stakeholders consulted in respect of possible social implications on Singaporeans arising from the proposed increases and, if so, who were these stakeholders?

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: These are our key partners because they are the people who are on the ground dealing with the issue of problem gambling, helping the families and the affected individuals.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: And when we discussed with them, they told us that they understood why we had to do this in a package.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: They welcomed the additional social safeguards that the Government will be introducing and, more importantly, there was a commitment that we should continue to work together hand in hand to help tackle the problem of gambling, including online gambling, new types of risks facing Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: We work hand in hand and we work together to help the affected individuals and their families.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: Were there any objections or reservations expressed by any of these stakeholders and, if so, who were they?

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: They understood why we had to do this as a package.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: They noted that the rate of problem gambling has been coming down but, as Minister Desmond Lee explained, just because the rate has come down does not mean that we, therefore, become complacent.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: We continue to take a serious view on how we can tackle this problem together.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: So, the community partners, the religious groups, the voluntary welfare groups said that they welcome the additional social safeguards, such as the increase in the levy, the additional safeguards.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Importantly, we need to continue to work together to tackle this problem hand in hand.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I do not think my question had been answered.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: How do you determine the land cost because this is without tender?

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The second question is: what is the projected revenue for the additional investments?

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: The second part of the question: of course, we made some projections, in terms of the increase in the number of visitors, tourists, what is the additional value-add to Singapore's economy.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: But the exact number depends also on the global economy, depends on how well we grow our tourism sector because the IRs are not the only thing we are going to develop to grow our tourism sector.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: We are looking at a new tourism site at Jurong Lake District and many others.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: [Pursuant to Standing Order No 22(3), provided that Members had not asked for questions standing in their names to be postponed to a later Sitting day or withdrawn, written answers to questions not reached by the end of Question Time are reproduced in the Appendix.]
